options.A: True (They manage the Scrum process and team effectiveness, though they do not manage people hierarchically).

questions.question: What happens if the Scrum Team cannot define a Sprint Goal during Sprint Planning?

options.A: They proceed without one and focus on the individual PBIs.
options.B: The Sprint should not start; the team must understand the 'Why' before committing to the 'What'.
options.C: The Product Owner assigns a default goal like 'Finish all tasks'.
options.D: The Scrum Master defines the goal for them to save time.

questions.question: Select ALL that apply: Which metrics are most helpful for a Scrum Team to track their own progress toward a Product Goal?

options.B: Individual lines of code per day.
options.D: Work Item Age (in the Sprint Backlog).

questions.question: What is the primary risk of a Product Owner who is too busy to collaborate with the Developers during the Sprint?

options.A: The Scrum Master will take over the Product Owner's role.
options.B: The Increments produced may not align with stakeholder needs, leading to wasted effort.
options.C: The Developers will have too much free time.
options.D: The Sprint Review will be cancelled.

questions.question: True or False: All Developers must attend the Sprint Review, even if they didn't finish their specific tasks.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following describes a 'Self-Managing' team?

options.A: The team chooses its own Product Owner and Scrum Master every Sprint.
options.B: The team decides internally who does what, when, and how.
options.C: The team operates without any constraints from the organization.
options.D: The team decides its own salary and working hours.

questions.question: How does 'Transparency' in Scrum support the pillar of 'Inspection'?

options.A: By allowing stakeholders to see the internal code of the product.
options.B: By ensuring the actual state of the artifacts is visible so that the inspection leads to valid results.
options.C: By forcing Developers to work in an open-plan office.
options.D: By publishing the team's velocity on the company's public website.

questions.question: Who is responsible for the 'Product Vision' in a Scrum environment?

options.B: The Product Owner.
options.D: The CEO.

questions.question: True or False: If an organization has a 'Release Management' team, the Scrum Team no longer needs a Definition of Done.

options.B: False (The Scrum Team always needs a DoD to ensure transparency of their Increment).

questions.question: If the Developers determine they have over-committed during the Sprint, what is the best immediate action?

options.A: They should work overtime to meet the initial commitment.
options.B: They should negotiate with the Product Owner to remove or adjust items while keeping the Sprint Goal intact.
options.C: They should cancel the Sprint and start a new Planning session.
options.D: They should inform the Scrum Master to assign less work in the next month.

questions.question: True or False: The Product Owner must be present at every Daily Scrum to provide directions to the Developers.

options.B: False (The Daily Scrum is for the Developers; the Product Owner only attends if they are also working on Sprint Backlog items).

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the Scrum Master's role during the Sprint Review?

options.A: They lead the demonstration of the product to the stakeholders.
options.B: They ensure the event takes place, stays within the timebox, and participants understand its purpose.
options.C: They act as the scribe, taking notes on all stakeholder feedback.
options.D: They approve the Increment before it is shown to the customers.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of 'Refinement' in the Product Backlog?

options.A: To create a detailed project schedule for the next six months.
options.B: To break down and further define Product Backlog items into smaller, more precise items.
options.C: To allow the Scrum Master to assign tasks to the Developers.
options.D: To ensure the Developers are working at 100% capacity.

questions.question: Who is responsible for the 'Definition of Done' if the organization does not have a standardized one?

options.B: The Product Owner
options.D: The Quality Assurance Manager

questions.question: True or False: The Scrum Master serves the Developers by coaching them in self-management and cross-functionality.

options.B: False

questions.question: Select ALL that apply: What are the three topics addressed during Sprint Planning?

options.B: What can be Done this Sprint?
options.C: How will the chosen work get done?
options.D: How much will the Sprint cost?

questions.question: What does 'Self-Managing' mean for a Scrum Team?

options.A: They decide who does what, when, and how internally.
options.B: They operate without any organizational oversight or budget.
options.C: They choose their own Product Owner every week.
options.D: They do not need to follow the Scrum Guide.

questions.question: Multiple teams are working on the same product. One team defines its own Definition of Done, which is less stringent than the others. What is the likely result?

options.A: The team will have a higher velocity, which is good for the project.
options.B: The transparency of the integrated Increment will be compromised, and hidden risks may emerge.
options.C: The other teams should lower their standards to match to ensure fairness.
options.D: The Scrum Master should fire the Developers on that team.

questions.question: A Product Owner is constantly adding new items to the Sprint Backlog during the Sprint. What should the Scrum Master do?

options.A: Nothing; the Product Owner is the boss of the Product Backlog.
options.B: Coach the Product Owner on the impact of changes to the Sprint Goal and the Developers' focus.
options.C: Tell the Developers to work faster to accommodate the new items.
options.D: Remove the Product Owner from the Scrum Team.

questions.question: True or False: Scrum is a 'Process' used to build a product.

options.B: False (Scrum is a 'Framework' within which you can employ various processes and techniques).

questions.question: What is the most effective way for a Scrum Master to help the organization adopt Scrum?

options.A: By forcing everyone to use specific software tools like Jira.
options.B: By leading, training, and coaching the organization in its Scrum adoption and planning Scrum implementations.
options.C: By acting as a Project Manager for all non-Scrum teams.
options.D: By ensuring the budget is always spent on time.

questions.question: During the Sprint Retrospective, the team identifies that the 'Definition of Done' is no longer sufficient for the product's quality needs. When should they update it?

options.A: At the start of the next release cycle.
options.B: Immediately; new items in the next Sprint must meet the updated, more stringent definition.
options.C: They shouldn't; only the organization can change the DoD.
options.D: After the Product Owner gets approval from the customer.

questions.question: Select ALL that apply: Which of the following are characteristics of the Product Goal?

options.A: It is the long-term objective for the Scrum Team.
options.B: The Scrum Team must fulfill one objective before taking on the next.
options.C: It is the commitment for the Product Backlog.
options.D: It is updated every Daily Scrum.

questions.question: What is the consequence of a Scrum Team not having a 'Done' Increment at the end of a Sprint?

options.A: They cannot hold a Sprint Review.
options.B: Transparency is lost, and the ability to inspect and adapt based on evidence is significantly reduced.
options.C: The Scrum Master must be replaced.
options.D: The Sprint is extended until the Increment is 'Done'.

questions.question: If a Scrum Team is unable to produce a 'Done' increment during a Sprint, what is the most significant impact?

options.A: The Scrum Master must manually approve the unfinished work.
options.B: The transparency of the product's actual progress is lost, hindering effective inspection and adaptation.
options.C: The Sprint is automatically extended by 24 hours.
options.D: The Developers must work on the unfinished items during the next Retrospective.

questions.question: Who is responsible for the 'Product Goal' and its transparency within the Product Backlog?

options.B: The Product Owner
options.D: The Developers

questions.question: True or False: The Scrum Team is expected to adapt their Definition of Done during the Sprint if they realize the current one is too difficult.

options.B: False (The DoD is usually inspected and adapted during the Sprint Retrospective to ensure consistency during the Sprint).

questions.question: What is the primary focus of 'Topic 1' during the Sprint Planning event?

options.A: Defining the technical tasks for each developer.
options.B: Establishing why the Sprint is valuable and defining the Sprint Goal.
options.C: Estimating the story points for the top backlog items.
options.D: Reviewing the budget for the upcoming month.

questions.question: During the Daily Scrum, the Developers notice a significant impediment that will prevent them from reaching the Sprint Goal. What should they do?

options.A: Wait until the Sprint Review to tell the Product Owner.
options.B: Immediately collaborate, potentially with the Scrum Master, to remove the impediment.
options.C: Remove the item from the Sprint Backlog without telling anyone.
options.D: Assign the blocker to the most junior developer to solve.

questions.question: Select ALL that apply: Which of the following are commitments for Scrum Artifacts?

options.B: Sprint Goal
options.D: Velocity

questions.question: True or False: Scrum defines 'Management' as an external role that oversees the Scrum Team's daily work.

options.B: False (Scrum Teams are self-managing; management's role is to support the environment for Scrum to flourish).

questions.question: In a 30-day Sprint, what is the maximum timebox for the Sprint Review?

options.B: 4 hours
options.D: 15 minutes

questions.question: Which role is responsible for the sizing of Product Backlog items?

options.B: The Developers
options.D: The Lead Architect

questions.question: What does 'Transparency' mean in the context of the Increment?

options.A: Stakeholders can see the source code at all times.
options.B: The state of the Increment is known and meets the Definition of Done so that those inspecting it can make valid decisions.
options.C: The developers' individual hours are logged in a public sheet.
options.D: The Product Owner shares the project budget with everyone.

questions.question: Who is responsible for the 'How' of the work during the Sprint?

options.B: The Developers
options.D: The Project Manager

questions.question: True or False: Multiple Scrum Teams working on the same product can have different Product Goals.

options.B: False (There is only one Product Goal and one Product Backlog for one product, regardless of the number of teams).

questions.question: Which event is a working session for the Scrum Team to inspect their people, relationships, process, and tools?

options.B: Sprint Retrospective
options.D: Sprint Review

questions.question: What is the commitment for the Product Backlog?

options.B: The Product Goal
options.D: The Release Plan

questions.question: True or False: The Scrum Master is a leader who serves the Scrum Team and the organization.

options.B: False

questions.question: What should the Developers do if they have too much time left before the end of the Sprint?

options.B: They should work with the Product Owner to pull in more items if the Sprint Goal is not endangered.
options.C: They should start working on the next Sprint without telling the Product Owner.
options.D: They should spend the time polishing features that were not requested.

questions.question: Which artifact is the Sprint Goal a part of?

options.B: Sprint Backlog
options.D: The Definition of Done

questions.question: Who defines the 'Definition of Done' if the organization does not have one?

options.B: The Scrum Team
options.D: The Developers

questions.question: True or False: The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.

options.B: False

questions.question: How long is the Daily Scrum if the team has 15 members?

options.B: 15 minutes
options.D: Scrum Teams should not have 15 members; they should be 10 or fewer.

questions.question: What is the commitment for the Increment?

options.B: The Definition of Done
options.D: The Release Candidate

questions.question: True or False: A Sprint is cancelled if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which pillar of empiricism is most associated with the Sprint Review?

options.B: Inspection
options.D: All of the above

questions.question: Who must attend the Sprint Retrospective?

options.A: Only the Developers and the Scrum Master.
options.B: The entire Scrum Team (Developers, Product Owner, Scrum Master).
options.D: The Scrum Team and the Stakeholders.

questions.question: True or False: The Sprint Backlog belongs solely to the Developers.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is the result of the Sprint Review?

options.B: A revised Product Backlog that defines the probable items for the next Sprint.
options.C: A final list of bugs to fix.
options.D: A signed contract for the next phase.

questions.question: Select ALL that apply: Which of the following are Scrum Values?

options.B: Focus
options.D: Trust

questions.question: True or False: The Product Owner determines how many items from the Product Backlog go into the Sprint.

options.B: False (The Developers select the items based on their capacity during Sprint Planning).

questions.question: Which role helps the Scrum Team focus on creating high-value Increments that meet the Definition of Done?

options.B: The Scrum Master
options.D: The Developers

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Product Goal?

options.A: To provide a 12-month roadmap for the team.
options.B: To serve as a long-term objective for the Scrum Team to plan against.
options.C: To replace the need for Sprint Goals.
options.D: To show the stakeholders the final project deadline.

questions.question: True or False: Product Backlog refinement is a mandatory formal Scrum event.

options.B: False (It is an ongoing activity to add detail, estimates, and order to items).

questions.question: What is the maximum duration of Sprint Planning for a one-month Sprint?

options.B: 8 hours
options.D: 12 hours

questions.question: Which role is responsible for eliminating impediments to the Scrum Team’s progress?

options.B: The Scrum Master
options.D: The HR Manager

questions.question: True or False: Every Increment must be released to production immediately after the Sprint Review.

options.B: False (It must be 'Done' and usable, but the decision to release is a business decision made by the Product Owner).

questions.question: What does a 'Cross-functional' team mean?

options.A: Team members work in different departments.
options.B: The team has all the skills necessary to create value each Sprint.
options.C: Team members rotate roles every month.
options.D: The team can work on any product in the company.

questions.question: Who manages the Sprint Backlog during the Sprint?

options.B: The Developers
options.D: The Team Lead

questions.question: True or False: The Scrum Master ensures the Daily Scrum stays within the 15-minute timebox.

options.B: False (The Developers are responsible for the Daily Scrum; the Scrum Master teaches them to keep it within the timebox).

questions.question: What happens to the remaining items in the Sprint Backlog if the Sprint ends?

options.B: They return to the Product Backlog and are re-evaluated.
options.C: They are automatically moved to the next Sprint.
options.D: They are deleted.

questions.question: Which Scrum Value is represented by the team being open about the work and the challenges?

options.B: Openness
options.D: Commitment

questions.question: True or False: The Scrum Master is responsible for the Developers' productivity.

options.B: False (The Scrum Master is responsible for the team's effectiveness by improving their practices within the Scrum framework).

questions.question: Who defines the 'What' during the Sprint Planning?

options.B: The Product Owner
options.D: The Stakeholders

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the Daily Scrum?

options.A: To provide a status report to the Product Owner.
options.B: To inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary.
options.C: To resolve all technical bugs found that morning.
options.D: To assign new tasks to the Developers.

questions.question: True or False: The Product Owner is responsible for the budget of the product.

options.B: False
